purpose: Public occupational-source baseline used to structure job-task-analysis review for the Technician I and Technician II cannabis cultivation credentials.
integrityBoundary: This is not a cannabis-specific job-task analysis and does not validate either credential. O*NET/BLS task families are adjacent national occupational evidence that must be reviewed, adapted, rejected or supplemented by cannabis cultivation SMEs/employers before occupational validation can be approved.

programs.interpretation: Technician I is aligned to routine crop/nursery/greenhouse work performed under established procedures, with cannabis-specific safety, traceability, biosecurity and authority boundaries layered on top.

taskFamilies.label: Observe crop condition and record crop/work information
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: National crop/nursery/greenhouse occupations include recording crop information and reporting crop progress.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: What cannabis-specific observations are expected at entry technician level?
Which records are regulatory/quality-critical versus general production records?
Which observations require escalation rather than diagnosis?

taskFamilies.label: Perform routine planting, transplanting, pruning and crop-care work
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: National crop/nursery/greenhouse work commonly includes planting, transplanting, pruning, weeding and other routine crop-care activities.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which routine cannabis canopy/propagation tasks belong at Technician I?
Which high-stress, chemical or specialized interventions remain outside scope?
What plant-identity controls must accompany movement or pruning?

taskFamilies.label: Execute routine irrigation and root-zone measurement work
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Crop/nursery/greenhouse roles include irrigation activities and use of irrigation equipment.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which irrigation checks can an entry technician perform independently?
Which pH/EC deviations require escalation?
Which equipment actions are operator-level versus maintenance?

taskFamilies.label: Scout crops and recognize pest/disease or abnormal-condition signals
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Crop occupations include inspecting plants and identifying pests/weeds as part of crop work.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: What level of pest/disease recognition is expected without diagnosing beyond evidence?
Which findings trigger quarantine/hold/escalation?
How are pesticide selection and application authority explicitly excluded unless separately qualified?

taskFamilies.label: Perform harvest, sorting, storage and postharvest handling
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: National crop occupations include harvesting plus inspection, grading, sorting, storage and postharvest handling.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which cannabis harvest/postharvest handoffs are Technician I responsibilities?
Which quality/disposition decisions remain outside scope?
What lot/plant identity and traceability controls are mandatory?

taskFamilies.label: Use tools/equipment safely and perform permitted operator-level care
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural workers commonly use crop-production equipment and may perform minor equipment work.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which checks are safe operator-level tasks?
Where must lockout/maintenance authority begin?
Which alarms or control failures require stop-work?

programs.interpretation: Technician II uses advanced monitoring, verification, troubleshooting, coordination and peer-support task families that overlap some agricultural supervisor work activities, while intentionally stopping short of general management, personnel authority, unrestricted maintenance, pesticide authority or final product disposition.

taskFamilies.label: Monitor crop and production systems and interpret abnormal conditions
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural supervisory work includes monitoring processes/materials/surroundings, inspecting crops and evaluating operational conditions.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which deviations can a Technician II troubleshoot within scope?
What evidence is required before changing a setpoint or work plan?
Which conditions require specialist, manager, QA or maintenance escalation?

taskFamilies.label: Verify safety, quality and procedure adherence during operations
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: First-line agricultural supervisors monitor operational quality/safety and inspect operations/equipment for problems.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which verification activities belong to a senior technician rather than a supervisor or QA authority?
How are observations documented without granting disciplinary or final-release authority?
Which safety conditions require immediate escalation?

taskFamilies.label: Inspect equipment/facilities and coordinate response to operating problems
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural supervisory/management sources include inspecting facilities/equipment and overseeing maintenance needs.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which verification tests can Technician II perform?
Which repairs require maintenance qualification or lockout?
How are sensor/equipment findings separated from unsupported root-cause claims?

taskFamilies.label: Coordinate work, priorities, records and shift handoff
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural supervisory work includes coordinating activities, schedules, information and operational decisions.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: What coordination can a senior technician perform without becoming a personnel supervisor?
Which decisions require manager approval?
What handoff evidence is necessary for traceability and unresolved risk?

taskFamilies.label: Provide bounded peer task support and procedure-based coaching
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural supervisory roles commonly train workers in crop work, equipment use and safety practices.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: What peer support is appropriate without granting formal trainer/authorization authority?
Which competencies require designated qualified trainers or assessors?
How is coaching separated from changing controlled procedures?

taskFamilies.label: Prepare evidence-based escalation and decision support for managers/QA/specialists
taskFamilies.publicOccupationalBasis: Agricultural supervisory work involves communicating with managers, evaluating conditions and supporting operational decisions.
cannabisAdaptationQuestions: Which evidence should Technician II assemble before escalation?
Which release/disposition/chemical/policy decisions remain outside the credential?
How should uncertainty and alternative explanations be communicated?
